items.action: Upgrade UnrealIRCd to 6.2.7.1 or apply the hot-patch; install the November Check Point Jumbo Hotfix (R82.20 Take 14, R82.10 Take 52, R82 Take 132 or R81.20 Take 174).
items.details: UnrealIRCd developers called CVE-2026-114713 their most critical security problem in 15 years; exploitation had already been observed online before the KEV listing. The Check Point flaw is a local privilege escalation to root in the DynamicCLI process, exploited since late October.
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 13: Check Point Gaia privilege escalation CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8) and UnrealIRCd server command injection CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS 8.6). Federal agencies must remediate by Monday, Nov 16.
items.title: CISA adds Check Point and UnrealIRCd flaws to KEV — patch by Nov 16

items.action: Apply the Nov 12 NetScaler ADC/Gateway and NetScaler Console updates.
items.details: The flaws are memory-corruption issues; none is reported exploited yet. CVE-2026-120868 affects every NetScaler ADC/Gateway deployment.
items.summary: Citrix fixed 28 vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway on Nov 12, including nine rated critical — among them NetScaler Console CVE-2026-120869 (CVSS 9.4).
items.title: Citrix patches 28 NetScaler flaws, nine critical

items.action: Upgrade Apache HTTP Server, or disable HTTP/2 until patched.
items.details: The flaw is a race condition leading to heap corruption; there is no workaround except disabling HTTP/2.
items.summary: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55–2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled (CVE-2026-119618) allows remote code execution via heap corruption.
items.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 RCE — patch or disable HTTP/2

items.details: The claim was tracked by Ransomware.live, discovered at 21:51 UTC on Nov 13. The compromised data is said to include internal records, financial documents, broker information, customer purchase details, invoices, passwords and 86GB of Outlook archives. Unverified claim.
items.summary: The Panzer ransomware group claimed on Nov 13 to have compromised RE/MAX Germany and exfiltrated 610GB of data, including passwords and Outlook archives.
items.title: Panzer claims RE/MAX Germany; says 610GB exfiltrated

items.details: The listing appeared on Akira's leak site on Nov 13. The group says it will upload 37GB of corporate data, including employee personal information (passports, medical information, driving licences, dates of birth), contracts, customer data and financials. Unverified claim.
items.summary: Akira listed Silicon Valley mechanical contractor Paragon Mechanical on its leak site on Nov 13, claiming 37GB of corporate data including employee PII.
items.title: Akira lists Paragon Mechanical, claims 37GB of data

items.details: The listing appeared on Akira's leak site on Nov 13. The group says it will upload 404GB of corporate data, including employee personal information (passports, driving licences and other HR files), contracts, customer data, financials and NDAs. Unverified claim.
items.summary: Akira also listed US globe manufacturer Replogle Globes on Nov 13, claiming 404GB of corporate data including employee PII and customer records.
items.title: Akira lists Replogle Globes, claims 404GB of data

items.action: Treat any SBI-related loan or account data as potentially circulating; watch for targeted phishing and fraudulent loan applications using KYC documents.
items.details: The FIR was registered at the CBD-Belapur police station on Nov 12 on a complaint from SBI official Bhavesh Nikam. The data is believed to contain customers' PII such as phone numbers and residential addresses, plus loan-application and account-opening paperwork. Police say the bank removed the stolen data from the dark web and that it was not misused; the case is booked under BNS sections and the IT Act.
items.summary: SBI has filed a police complaint after hackers operating as 'Siriusim' allegedly accessed its Global IT Centre in Navi Mumbai between Oct 10–15 and stole about 3.75 lakh customer records, later spotted on the dark web.
items.title: SBI files FIR as 3.75 lakh records surface on dark web

items.action: NBFCs and fintechs should lock down payout and disbursement APIs, isolate test/staging environments, rotate shared credentials and monitor for small test transfers.
items.details: Three Telangana-based lenders reported 304 fraudulent transactions between Oct 19 and Nov 6; Hyderabad-based VIVIFI detected 183 fraudulent transactions worth ₹3.34 crore within 88 minutes on Oct 19. Similar attacks were reported in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Delhi, Chandigarh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. CERT-In's Nov 4 advisory (CIAD-2026-0058) flagged the AI-assisted 'Crafty Falcon' campaign exploiting exposed test systems, shared credentials and payment APIs.
items.summary: AI-assisted cyberattacks on India's smaller NBFCs have siphoned off nearly ₹300 crore in two months, with hackers turning payout APIs into theft routes — starting with ₹1 test transfers before draining accounts.
items.title: NBFC payout-API raids cost nearly ₹300 crore in two months
